events.title: The fall of Robespierre and the end of the Terror
events.shortBlurb: The execution of Robespierre brought the Reign of Terror to a close and eased the persecution of the Church…
body: Maximilien Robespierre, born at Arras in 1758, rose through the Jacobin Club to dominate the Committee of Public Safety in the year of the Terror. On 8 June 1794 he presided over the Festival of the Supreme Being, the deist cult he had raised in place of the Church; two days later the Law of 22 Prairial stripped the Revolutionary Tribunal of every defense.

In the seven weeks that followed, the Paris guillotine claimed more than thirteen hundred lives. The Church suffered bitterly in those years, her refractory priests deported or drowned, and on 17 July 1794 sixteen Carmelite nuns of Compiègne mounted the scaffold singing, martyrs beatified in 1906.

On 27 July, 9 Thermidor, the Convention turned on him, voted his arrest, and outlawed him; cornered that night in the Hôtel de Ville, his jaw shattered by a pistol shot, he was guillotined the next evening, 28 July, with twenty-one of his partisans, among them Saint-Just and Couthon. His death broke the machinery of the Terror, and the persecution of the Church slowly eased.
